messages:
Maria: Dropping a quick pass on the model catalog compare panel. I sketched two alternate approaches for density toggles, pinned versions visibility, and the small performance sparklines. Link: https://figma.com/s/xys (draft).
Todd: nice. what's the main tradeoff between the two approaches?
Maria: Short: Variant A keeps compact rows (helps see more models) but moves sparklines into a hover reveal and shrinks badges to 10px height. Variant B increases row height by 10px, surfaces sparklines inline, and uses 13px badges with slightly darker fills.
Rachel: accessibility-first take: Variant A's hover-only sparklines are invisible to keyboard and screen reader users. If we hide visual sparklines behind hover we must provide an aria-describedby summary like "Latency: median 120ms; trend stable".
Evan: also a discoverability issue: if sparklines are hover-only, mobile users won't see them at all. I'd prefer inline mini-sparklines for everyone, maybe with an optional density toggle that collapses them.
Maria: Agreed. Proposal: default to inline mini-sparkline + badge; add a density toggle in the header: Compact / Comfortable. Compact hides sparkline and reduces vertical padding; Comfortable shows sparkline and 13px badges. Save user choice in preferences.
Todd: nice. Another UI nit: when pinning a version we currently render a small star icon that blends into the right-side action menu. Users reported missing pinned rows when they return. Suggest we promote pinned state to the left of the row with a visible "Pinned" label and a subtle background tint.
Rachel: promote + accessibility: Make the pinned control first in the tab order and ensure the pinned state is announced by screen readers on load via aria-live region: "X pinned models shown". Also ensure contrast of the tint meets AA.
Evan: implementation caveat: promoting the pin to the left changes column widths and might shift content causing layout jump when toggling. Could freeze the left column or reserve the pin column always to avoid reflow.
Maria: good call. We'll reserve a 36px left column for pin/check icons. That avoids reflow and makes keyboard targets consistent.
Todd: copy micro-issue: the current badge hover shows "cost" — ambiguous. Recommend: "Cost estimate (per-1k tokens)" and include a tiny info icon linking to billing docs. Also for sparklines, tooltip should say "p50 over 24h" or similar.
Rachel: keyboard flow proposal: tab order should be left reserved pin -> compare checkbox -> model name -> badges -> actions. Use visible focus rings and focus-visible only styles. Add a "Compare selected (n)" sticky toolbar when any compare checkbox is selected so screen reader users know context.
Evan: performance UX: show a tiny delta indicator next to sparklines for regressions e.g. +12% (red up arrow). That needs color + icon — but do not rely on color only. Add aria-labels e.g. "Latency increased 12 percent".
Maria: color palette for badges: Current suggestion from design: Latency bg #1f6f4a (white text), Throughput bg #0f6b99 (white text), Cost bg #ffd166 (dark text). Rachel, can you verify contrast for those at 13px?
Rachel: I'll run contrast checks. Quick reaction: #ffd166 with dark text might be borderline on some monitors. We can add a 1px stroke or increase text weight. Also ensure all badge elements have role="status" and aria-live="polite" when they update in place.
Todd: dev estimate please? Pin column + preferences persistence + density toggle + sparklines inline = medium (3-4 dev days) assuming we reuse existing prefs infra and chart primitives. Delta indicators + aria-live messaging small.
Evan: small technical note: inline sparklines in each row can add DOM nodes; consider rendering via canvas layer or a virtualized sparkline renderer to avoid layout/paint churn in large lists.
Maria: UX acceptance criteria (draft):
- Density toggle in header persists per-user.
- Pinned models show left-most "Pinned" label and are first in tab order.
- Inline sparklines visible in Comfortable mode; hidden in Compact but accessible via aria-description.
- Badges meet contrast >= 4.5:1 and include aria-labels with metric context.
- Keyboard order: pin -> compare -> name -> badges -> actions.
- Regression delta indicated with icon + text and announced to screen readers when value changes.
Todd: I'll open the ticket with ACs + attach Maria's Figma variants. We'll tag eng and accessibility for review.
ux-bot: Reminder: Accessibility review board meets Fri 2pm. Please attach final specs by Thu EOD.
Rachel: i'll validate colors and draft the aria examples in the ticket. Also will mock NVDA readout for the pinned/compare flow.
Evan: i'll prototype a canvas-based sparkline renderer and report perf numbers.
Maria: thanks all 0. I'll update Figma and leave comments on the exact pixel sizes.
Todd: thanks team. Follow-up thread in ticket once the sketches are attached.
